title: Resistivity; Electrical power and energy

Terms and clues: EL05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; EL04-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; EL04-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game. assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Power
items.clue: Rate of energy transfer, which can be found from I²R.

items.label: Crocodile clip
items.clue: Sliding connector that sets the length of wire being tested.

items.label: Series
items.clue: Arrangement in which a kettle element and its cable carry the same current.

items.label: Voltmeter
items.clue: Instrument connected across the chosen length of wire, giving V for R = V/I.

questions.stem: A student plots R against length for a uniform wire of diameter 0.40 mm. The best-fit line has a gradient of 4.0 Ω m⁻¹ and crosses the R axis at 0.30 Ω. What is the resistivity of the wire?
questions.explanation: A = π(0.40 × 10⁻³)²/4 = 1.26 × 10⁻⁷ m². ρ = gradient × A = 4.0 × 1.26 × 10⁻⁷ = 5.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m. The 0.30 Ω intercept (contact resistance) does not affect the gradient.

questions.stem: The potential difference across an ohmic resistor is increased so that the current in the resistor becomes three times as large. What is the ratio of the new power dissipated in the resistor, P₂, to the original power, P₁?
questions.explanation: The resistor is ohmic, so R is unchanged. P = I²R: tripling I multiplies P by 3² = 9.

questions.stem: A copper wire and a sample of pure silicon, a semiconductor, are both cooled from 20 °C to −20 °C. How does the resistance of each change, and why?

options.text: Copper's falls: less ion vibration. Silicon's rises: fewer charge carriers.
Both fall, as the ions in each vibrate less, so there are fewer collisions.
Copper's falls, as fewer electrons are freed; silicon's rises, as its ions vibrate more.
Both rise, since cooling makes the charge carriers in each move more slowly.

questions.explanation: Right. In copper the carrier number hardly changes, so fewer collisions win. In silicon the carrier number drops sharply, which outweighs the smaller vibration.

questions.stem: A steady current of 0.25 A flows in a 24 Ω resistor for 2.0 minutes. How much energy is dissipated in the resistor?
questions.explanation: Power = I²R = 0.25² × 24 = 1.5 W. Energy = power × time = 1.5 W × 120 s = 180 J.

questions.stem: An unlabelled wire has a mean diameter of 0.32 mm. Its resistance between the clips is 1.72 Ω at a length of 0.20 m and 5.37 Ω at 0.80 m. Resistivities: copper 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m; iron 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; constantan 4.9 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; nichrome 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m. Which metal is the wire most likely made of?
A 3.0 kW kettle is switched on for 4.0 minutes. How much energy does it transfer, in kWh?
A 60 W lamp and a 100 W lamp are both rated for a 230 V supply. They are connected in series across a 230 V supply. Assume each keeps its normal working resistance. Which lamp is brighter?

options.text: The 60 W lamp: it has the larger resistance, and in series both carry the same current.
The 100 W lamp: it has the higher power rating, so it gives more light.
The 100 W lamp: a smaller resistance gives more power, as P = V²/R.
Both are equally bright, as they carry the same current.

questions.explanation: R = V²/P: about 880 Ω for the 60 W lamp, 530 Ω for the 100 W lamp. Same current in series, so P = I²R is larger in the 60 W lamp (about 23 W against 14 W).
